channel.title: Daily Intel Brief
channel.description: Daily open-source summary of global geopolitics, military and economic affairs.

item.title: Daily Intel Brief — 17 November 2026
item.description: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait Bridge for a second straight night, collapsing a section of the automobile road span into the sea while Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv's Northern and Southern Dnipro bridges and disrupted water, heating and metro services. Under Interim CEO Colette Kress, NVIDIA beat Wall Street with $115.8 billion in Q3 revenue (+103% YoY), $107.6 billion in Data Center sales and $130.0 billion Q4 guidance excluding China — after the Dow fell 1.64% to 50,759 and 10-year Treasury yields climbed to 5.14% during regular trading. Trump arrived in Manila for the US–ASEAN Special Summit amid protests over Washington's Pax Silica chip-minerals initiative before heading to Shenzhen for APEC, while EU defence ministers backed Ukraine's plan to double 2027 drone supplies after a €1.71bn Commission disbursement. The LPG carrier Tara Gas was abandoned off Oman with one Indian seafarer missing after a second strike as US warplanes bombed an Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island; meanwhile CISA urged immediate patching for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), Equinor confirmed an active cyberattack, and an Optimizely JS attack hit 178 major sites.

item.title: Daily Intel Brief — 16 November 2026
item.description: Trump departed for Manila and Shenzhen ahead of the 19 November trilateral with Xi and Putin, while US envoys held difficult remote Ukraine talks with Kyiv and Europeans — only for Moscow to say the next round will remain strictly trilateral without Europe. Washington closed its third-country AI data-center compute loophole across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil in direct response to the Jensen Huang scandal. Nvidia fell 4.12% to $156.14 and the Nasdaq dropped 2.49% ahead of Tuesday's earnings. Infrastructure warfare escalated in both theatres: Ukrainian drones struck the Kerch Bridge twice inside 24 hours and hit Russia's Ilsky refinery, while Russian ballistic missiles struck two Dnipro bridges in Kyiv; in the Gulf, a third US carrier entered the theatre as UKMTO logged two Hormuz tanker attacks. Google Threat Intelligence Group exposed the first human-out-of-the-loop patch-to-exploit AI framework (exploit_agent), while SpaceX blamed a 'technical issue' for five days of Starshield throttling along Ukraine's front lines.

item.title: Daily Intel Brief — 15 November 2026
item.description: The trilateral is on for 19 November in Shenzhen — nuclear arms and Iran on the agenda, Ukraine explicitly off it. In parallel, Zelensky disclosed that Washington floated Ukraine ceding the Donbas in exchange for NATO membership. The two tracks are pulling apart: one is great-power theatre, the other a hard territorial bargain Kyiv has not accepted. Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned over an affair with a woman US intelligence assesses as a Chinese agent. The AI trade is de-rating — Nvidia's sixth straight down week, semiconductors off 3.4% — and the company reports Q3 earnings on 17 November under an interim CEO. A national-security story wearing a market costume. Ukraine's deep-strike campaign is compounding: a tenth Russian refinery hit in two weeks, radar kills that induced Russian friendly fire, and a third fuel crisis in a year. Hormuz added a third tanker-mine claim in 48 hours, while the IAEA says it has lost continuity of knowledge over Iran's enriched-uranium stock. Gaza's ceasefire is being eroded by strikes and winter, not by a formal collapse: 17 states condemned the Nasser Hospital strike, flooding has hit over 100,000 people, and Israel's aid restrictions persist.

item.title: Daily Intel Brief — 14 November 2026
item.description: The White House confirmed the first-ever US–China–Russia trilateral, on the APEC sidelines in Shenzhen on 19 November. Symbolism will outweigh substance, but it puts all three leaders in one room while the Ukraine file stalls. Ukraine: the Kremlin is reaching for a rewritten European security architecture — the December 2021 draft treaties — while the EU calls it a trap and insists on sequencing. Starshield throttling is now failing 100% of Ukrainian interceptor missions. The IEA declared the global oil market back in surplus in Q4 for the first time since the Iran war began. Brent has fallen from $136 to the mid-$90s; diesel remains ~77% above pre-war. Gaza's ceasefire is formally alive and functionally frozen — disarmament-versus-withdrawal deadlock, winter flooding, and a 53-state demand for aid entry.
